metais skill — Write metais's agent skill, which teaches a coding agent the
golden paths, where the agent's harness reads skills.

Usage:
  metais skill [--harness <name>]... [--dir <dir>] [--overwrite] [--dry-run]
               [--print] [--json]

Writes SKILL.md, the skill a coding agent's harness loads before its first
command, to .claude/skills/metais/ for Claude Code, or to .agents/skills/metais/
for Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and OpenCode, beneath the directory --dir names:
the current directory when it is omitted. The skill's text is part of metais and
versioned with it.

Without --harness, the harness is the one the directory shows: .claude/ or
.agents/. When it holds neither, or both, metais skill writes nothing and asks
for --harness. Both directories are written only when --harness names a harness
of each.

A harness finds a project's skills from the directory it starts in up to the
repository's top level, so run metais skill there; a directory with no .git
entry gets a warning. For every project of your own, write --dir ~, with a
space: a shell does not expand the ~ of --dir=~.

Each SKILL.md ends with a line naming the version that wrote it and the digest
of the text above it. Running metais skill again replaces a copy metais wrote
that nobody edited, when its version or text differs, and leaves an edited copy
as it is unless --overwrite is given. --dry-run reports what each target needs,
so it says whether the skill is current.

Flags:
  --harness <name>
      The harness to write the skill for: claude writes .claude/skills, and
      codex, gemini, cursor and opencode write .agents/skills. Detected from the
      directory when omitted. Values: claude, codex, gemini, cursor, opencode.
      May be given more than once.
  --dir <dir>
      The existing directory to write beneath, the current directory when
      omitted: a repository's top level, or ~ for your own scope, written --dir
      ~ with a space.
  --overwrite
      Replace a skill someone edited, or one metais did not write.
  --dry-run
      Report what each target needs, and write nothing.
  --print
      Print the skill to standard output, and write nothing; it takes no other
      flag but --json.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  Each SKILL.md written, or that would be, with what was done to it and the
  harnesses that read it; with --print, the skill itself. With --json, one
  metais.skill/1 document.

Refusals:
  output.destination.link
      A symbolic link stands at, or above, a target beneath the directory.
      Next: metais skill --print
  output.destination.not_directory
      The directory, or a directory a target needs, is not a directory.
      Next: metais skill
  output.destination.not_regular_file
      A directory or special file stands at a target's SKILL.md.
      Next: metais skill
  output.destination.nothing_written
      The directory cannot be opened, or a write failed before any target was
      written.
      Next: metais skill
  output.destination.write_failed
      A write failed after another target was written, which is left in place.
      Next: metais skill
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais skill --help
  usage.flag_excluded
      --print is given with another of metais skill's flags.
      Next: metais skill --help
  usage.harness_required
      No --harness is given, and the directory holds neither or both of .claude/
      and .agents/.
      Next: metais skill --harness claude
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais skill --help
  usage.skill_edited
      A SKILL.md metais did not write, or one edited since, stands at a target.
      Next: metais skill --overwrite
  usage.unexpanded_tilde
      --dir's value begins with a literal ~, as --dir=~ gives it.
      Next: metais skill --dir ~
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais skill --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais skill --help

Examples:
  metais skill --harness claude
      Writes .claude/skills/metais/SKILL.md beneath the current directory, for
      Claude Code.
  metais skill
      Writes the skill for the harness the current directory shows, .claude/ or
      .agents/.
  metais skill --harness claude --harness codex
      Writes it for Claude Code and for the harnesses that read .agents/skills.
  metais skill --harness claude --dir ~
      Writes it to ~/.claude/skills, for every project of yours.
  metais skill --dry-run
      Reports whether the skill is current, and writes nothing.
  metais skill --print
      Prints the skill, for a harness that reads skills from somewhere else.
